title: Genie Chance and the Great Alaska Earthquake

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Well, I suppose you want to know where I was when this disaster took place.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想你一定想知道这场灾难发生时我在哪里。

sentences.en: I was driving on my way home, and I began to feel that the car I had just purchased was a lemon because the wheels appeared to be running off the car.
sentences.zh: 我当时正开车回家，开始觉得我刚买的那辆车是个次品，因为车轮看起来好像要从车上掉下来了。

sentences.en: I managed to stop the car, and I looked in stupefaction at the road about ten feet ahead of me and saw the road break open.
sentences.zh: 我设法把车停下，惊愕地看着前方约十英尺处的路面，看到路面裂开了。

sentences.en: And then, like two big halves of a huge sandwich, start moving like scissors back and forth, one half moving in one direction, the other half moving in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 然后，就像一个巨大三明治的两半，开始像剪刀一样来回移动，一半向一个方向移动，另一半向另一个方向移动。

sentences.en: And all the time, while watching the road, it suddenly dawned on me that this was not an ordinary disaster, that it was perhaps one of the greatest disasters to hit North America.
sentences.zh: 一直盯着路面看的时候，我突然意识到这不是一场普通的灾难，这可能是袭击北美最严重的灾难之一。

sentences.en: I kept thinking, what will Alaskans do now?
sentences.zh: 我一直在想，阿拉斯加人现在该怎么办？

sentences.en: What will Alaskans do now?
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加人现在该怎么办？

sentences.en: There are moments when the world we take for granted instantaneously changes, when reality is abruptly upended and the unimaginable overwhelms real life.
sentences.zh: 有些时刻，我们认为理所当然的世界会瞬间改变，现实被突然颠覆，不可想象的事情淹没了现实生活。

sentences.en: We don't walk around thinking about that instability, but we know it's always there.
sentences.zh: 我们平时不会去想这种不稳定性，但我们知道它一直存在。

sentences.en: At random and without warning, a kind of terrible magic can switch on and scramble our lives.
sentences.zh: 随机且毫无预兆地，一种可怕的魔力可能会开启并打乱我们的生活。

sentences.en: You may know the feeling.
sentences.zh: 你可能了解这种感觉。

sentences.en: In 1964, it happened to Anchorage, Alaska, and to a woman named Jeannie Chance.
sentences.zh: 1964年，这种事发生在阿拉斯加安克雷奇，发生在一个叫珍妮·钱斯的女人身上。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: The Great Alaska Earthquake was the biggest earthquake to ever hit North America.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加大地震是北美有史以来发生的最大地震。

sentences.en: John Moella, author of the book This Is Chance, on the story of that disaster, and the voice that held the state together.
sentences.zh: 《这就是钱斯》一书的作者约翰·莫埃拉，讲述了那场灾难的故事，以及那个将整个州凝聚在一起的声音。

sentences.en: It's Friday, May 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月22日，星期五。

sentences.en: Sunday, February 23rd, 1964.
sentences.zh: 1964年2月23日，星期日。

sentences.en: A month before the earthquake.
sentences.zh: 地震发生前一个月。

sentences.en: Just before 1 p.m.
sentences.zh: 下午1点前。

sentences.en: The deciding heat of the world championship sled dog races was about to start.
sentences.zh: 世界锦标赛雪橇犬比赛的决胜赛段即将开始。

sentences.en: They have estimated the crowd as high as 12,000 people.
sentences.zh: 据估计，人群多达12000人。

sentences.en: And all of Anchorage, it seemed, had gathered downtown to watch.
sentences.zh: 似乎整个安克雷奇的人都聚集在市中心观看比赛。

sentences.en: And this is the one time of the year, the only time of the year, we ever get that many people into Alaska's largest city.
sentences.zh: 这是每年唯一一次，也是一年中唯一一次，我们能让这么多人聚集在阿拉斯加最大的城市。

sentences.en: And I think it's a wonderful thing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一件美妙的事情。

sentences.en: The races were one of the longest-running traditions in a community that didn't have a lot of traditions yet.
sentences.zh: 在当时一个还没什么传统的社区里，这些比赛是历史最悠久的传统之一。

sentences.en: Something for the fledgling city to look forward to in the coldest, loneliest stretch of winter.
sentences.zh: 这是这座新兴城市在冬天最寒冷、最孤独的时段里所期待的事情。

sentences.en: Yes, you are.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Thanks to the city of Anchorage.
sentences.zh: 感谢安克雷奇市。

sentences.en: We'll be back with more after this important message.
sentences.zh: 在这条重要信息之后，我们将回来继续报道。

sentences.en: Buckle up, foreign safety.
sentences.zh: 系好安全带，为了安全。

sentences.en: Buckle up.
sentences.zh: 系好安全带。

sentences.en: Anchorage, Alaska, in 1964, was a blotch of Western civilization in the middle of emptiness.
sentences.zh: 1964年的阿拉斯加安克雷奇，就像荒原中一点西方文明的斑点。

sentences.en: Alaska had only become the country's 49th state five years earlier.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加五年前才刚刚成为美国的第49个州。

sentences.en: And it was often disregarded as a kind of free-floating addendum to the rest of America.
sentences.zh: 它经常被视为美国其余部分的一个自由漂浮的附录而被忽视。

sentences.en: But Anchorage was Alaska's biggest and proudest city.
sentences.zh: 但安克雷奇是阿拉斯加最大、最引以为傲的城市。

sentences.en: A community whose essential spirit, one visitor wrote, reached aggressively and greedily to grasp the future.
sentences.zh: 一位游客写道，这是一个本质精神积极且贪婪地想要抓住未来的社区。

sentences.en: Impatient with any suggestion that such things take time.
sentences.zh: 对任何认为这些事情需要时间的建议都感到不耐烦。

sentences.en: It was a modern-day frontier town that imagined it was a metropolis.
sentences.zh: 这是一个现代边境小镇，却自以为是一座大都市。

sentences.en: Okay, back here with more action.
sentences.zh: 好了，回到这里继续关注更多赛事动态。

sentences.en: Straining to make itself real.
sentences.zh: 努力让这一切变得真实。

sentences.en: Here's the countdown now.
sentences.zh: 现在开始倒计时。

sentences.en: Five, four, three, eight.
sentences.zh: 五，四，三，八。

sentences.en: Okay, there we go.
sentences.zh: 好了，开始了。

sentences.en: It's one o'clock dog-mushing time.
sentences.zh: 一点钟，雪橇犬比赛时间到了。

sentences.en: Keith Breyer is off to a real fine start.
sentences.zh: 基思·布雷耶开局非常不错。

sentences.en: Eleven dogs lining up very nicely right here.
sentences.zh: 十一只狗在这里排得非常整齐。

sentences.en: A local radio station, KE and I, was covering the races.
sentences.zh: 当地广播电台KENI正在报道这场比赛。

sentences.en: Keith Breyer should be out to 15th and Cordova.
sentences.zh: 基思·布雷耶现在应该到了第15街和科尔多瓦街路口。

sentences.en: Let's go down to Jeannie Chance.
sentences.zh: 让我们连线珍妮·钱斯。

sentences.en: Come in, please.
sentences.zh: 请回答。

sentences.en: Jeannie.
sentences.zh: 珍妮。

sentences.en: And threw the broadcast to a part-time reporter named Jeannie Chance.
sentences.zh: 并将广播转交给了一位兼职记者，名叫珍妮·钱斯。

sentences.en: Yes, here is Jeannie Chance at 15th and Cordova.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是珍妮·钱斯，现在在第15街和科尔多瓦街路口。

sentences.en: We'd just gotten set up at a radio checkpoint at the top of Cordova Hill.
sentences.zh: 我们刚在科尔多瓦山顶的一个广播检查站架设好设备。

sentences.en: About a block and a half away from it.
sentences.zh: 距离那里大约一个半街区。

sentences.en: Right as the sleds dashed by.
sentences.zh: 就在雪橇疾驰而过的时候。

sentences.en: And he is running strong.
sentences.zh: 他跑得很有劲。

sentences.en: The crowd together...
sentences.zh: 人群一起……

sentences.en: Jeannie was relieved she'd made it in time.
sentences.zh: 珍妮很庆幸自己及时赶到了。

sentences.en: She was the only woman covering the event for KE and I, and her bosses had given her a tough assignment.
sentences.zh: 她是KENI电台唯一报道此事的女性，她的老板给她布置了一个艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: It's the largest crowd we've had at this checkpoint.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在这个检查站遇到的人数最多的一次。

sentences.en: She'd started the day at a spot at the beginning of the course, but once she'd broadcast her play-by-play there,
sentences.zh: 她当天早些时候在赛道起点处开始工作，但一旦她在那里完成了现场直播，

sentences.en: she had to scramble along a few miles of icy roads to this checkpoint, further along the route.
sentences.zh: 她就必须沿着几英里的冰雪路面匆忙赶到这个位于赛道更远处的检查站。

sentences.en: Here they come through, they're running strong.
sentences.zh: 他们过来了，跑得很有劲。

sentences.en: Before the dogs plowed by her again.
sentences.zh: 在狗群再次从她身边飞驰而过之前。

sentences.en: Beautiful people.
sentences.zh: 可爱的人们。

sentences.en: But she'd made it.
sentences.zh: 但她还是赶上了。

sentences.en: Because professionally, Jeannie Chance was relentless.
sentences.zh: 因为在职业操守上，珍妮·钱斯从不懈怠。

sentences.en: And this is Jeannie Chance, returning at the Cordova Center.
sentences.zh: 我是珍妮·钱斯，现在回到科尔多瓦中心。

sentences.en: She had to be.
sentences.zh: 她必须如此。

sentences.en: Jeannie was said to be the first female newscaster in Alaska.
sentences.zh: 据说珍妮是阿拉斯加第一位女性新闻主播。

sentences.en: At 37 years old, she was strikingly beautiful, with short, wavy blonde hair and high-cut bangs.
sentences.zh: 37岁的她长得非常漂亮，留着短而卷曲的金发，剪着高刘海。

sentences.en: She grew up in a small town in Texas, where she'd met her husband Winston and had three kids.
sentences.zh: 她在德克萨斯州的一个小镇长大，在那里遇到了丈夫温斯顿，并生了三个孩子。

sentences.en: There, Winston sold used cars, but he wasn't particularly good at it.
sentences.zh: 温斯顿在那里卖二手车，但他并不擅长。

sentences.en: Even when he did manage to land a commission, he had a habit of blowing it on a steak dinner and drinks before he got home.
sentences.zh: 即使他设法赚到佣金，他也习惯在回家前把钱花在牛排晚餐和酒水上。

sentences.en: The financial strain started to destabilize their marriage, and the pressure fell on Jeannie to hold the family together and make their precarious life feel safe.
sentences.zh: 经济压力开始动摇他们的婚姻，维持家庭、让不稳定的生活感到安全，这些重担都落在了珍妮身上。

sentences.en: We're not poor, she'd tell her children.
sentences.zh: 我们并不穷，她会告诉孩子们。

sentences.en: We just don't have any money.
sentences.zh: 我们只是没钱而已。

sentences.en: At the time, a wave of young Texans was decamping for jobs in Alaska, and Winston was convinced it was a land of opportunity, where anyone willing to work could wind up flush.
sentences.zh: 当时，一批年轻的德克萨斯人正动身前往阿拉斯加寻找工作，温斯顿坚信那是一片充满机遇的土地，任何愿意工作的人都能发财。

sentences.en: But Jeannie hesitated.
sentences.zh: 但珍妮犹豫了。

sentences.en: Alaska didn't sound like a fun adventure to her.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加听起来对她来说不是什么有趣的冒险。

sentences.en: It sounded desolate and dreadful, like moving to the moon.
sentences.zh: 听起来荒凉而可怕，就像搬到月球上一样。

sentences.en: Then again, if life didn't improve for her and Winston in Anchorage, maybe divorce might feel a little more feasible there.
sentences.zh: 话又说回来，如果她和温斯顿在安克雷奇的生活没有好转，也许在那里离婚会更容易一些。

sentences.en: She'd be at the edge of the world.
sentences.zh: 她将身处世界的边缘。

sentences.en: Nobody would have to know.
sentences.zh: 没人会知道。

sentences.en: But Alaska didn't solve Winston's troubles with money.
sentences.zh: 但阿拉斯加并没有解决温斯顿的经济问题。

sentences.en: And before long, the Chance family was unable to pay the rent.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，钱斯一家就付不起房租了。

sentences.en: Winston said not to worry.
sentences.zh: 温斯顿说不用担心。

sentences.en: He'd sell some cars soon.
sentences.zh: 他很快就能卖掉几辆车。

sentences.en: Jeannie worried.
sentences.zh: 珍妮很担心。

sentences.en: And this is what a good wife is supposed to do, she wrote.
sentences.zh: 她写道，这就是好妻子应该做的吗？

sentences.en: Just wait at home for her man to bring money in to pay the bills and feed the family?
sentences.zh: 只是在家里等着丈夫带钱回来付账单、养活家庭？

sentences.en: If other wives do it all the time, why can't I learn to relax and let it happen?
sentences.zh: 如果其他妻子都能做到，为什么我不能学会放松，顺其自然呢？

sentences.en: She went to Winston weeping one day, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，有一天她哭着去找温斯顿。

sentences.en: And he told her,
sentences.zh: 他却对她说，

sentences.en: Well, if you're so worried about paying the rent, why are you sitting on your fat fanny?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你这么担心付房租，为什么还坐在那里无所事事？

sentences.en: Get out there and get a job.
sentences.zh: 出去找份工作吧。

sentences.en: Jeannie was speechless.
sentences.zh: 珍妮哑口无言。

sentences.en: Two weeks later, she got herself hired at KENI.
sentences.zh: 两周后，她成功在KENI电台找到了工作。

sentences.en: Coming up, Cordova Hill.
sentences.zh: 接下来是科尔多瓦山。

sentences.en: Let's go out to Jeannie Chan.
sentences.zh: 让我们连线珍妮·钱斯。

sentences.en: At the time, women broadcasters typically covered fashion and homemaking, or hosted on-air recipe swaps.
sentences.zh: 当时，女性广播员通常报道时尚和家政，或者主持直播间的食谱交换节目。

sentences.en: But in her year and a half at the station,
sentences.zh: 但在电台工作的一年半里，

sentences.en: Jeannie had forged a role for herself as an industrious, roving reporter.
sentences.zh: 珍妮为自己开辟了一个勤奋、奔波的记者角色。

sentences.en: She covered crime in the courts, in City Hall.
sentences.zh: 她报道法院和市政厅的犯罪新闻。

sentences.en: She reported from crab boats and missile sites, burning buildings in Inuit villages, and sled dog races.
sentences.zh: 她从捕蟹船、导弹基地、燃烧的建筑物、因纽特村庄和雪橇犬比赛现场进行报道。

sentences.en: During the final stretch of the race,
sentences.zh: 在比赛的最后阶段，

sentences.en: Jeannie lost herself in the excitement a little,
sentences.zh: 珍妮有点沉浸在兴奋之中，

sentences.en: and just started shouting,
sentences.zh: 开始大喊大叫，

sentences.en: Oh, and yes, into her microphone as the mushers passed.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，当雪橇手经过时，她对着麦克风喊道。

sentences.en: And another KENI broadcaster appeared to make a sly, off-color crack about her breathlessness on the air.
sentences.zh: 另一位KENI广播员似乎对她在直播中气喘吁吁的样子开了个狡猾、低俗的玩笑。

sentences.en: Jeannie tried to be gracious and stoic, to do what was expected of her without complaint.
sentences.zh: 珍妮试图表现得大度而坚忍，不抱怨地完成份内工作。

sentences.en: She figured this was the only way to diffuse the discomfort of the men around her.
sentences.zh: 她认为这是缓解周围男性尴尬的唯一方法。

sentences.en: At the end of the sled dog races that afternoon, she'd sign off by thanking not only all the KENI listeners and spectators,
sentences.zh: 那天下午雪橇犬比赛结束时，她不仅感谢了所有KENI的听众和观众，

sentences.en: but her male co-workers too.
sentences.zh: 还感谢了她的男性同事。

sentences.en: I want to thank you too, Al Bramstead, Ty Clark, and Bob Fleming, for allowing this little gal to be a part of the biggest broadcast crew ever attend.
sentences.zh: 我也要感谢你们，阿尔·布拉姆斯特德、泰·克拉克和鲍勃·弗莱明，感谢你们让这个小姑娘成为有史以来规模最大的广播团队的一员。

sentences.en: And she was also sure to thank her husband
sentences.zh: 她还特意感谢了她的丈夫，

sentences.en: for his permission.
sentences.zh: 感谢他的许可。

sentences.en: Now back to Sutton West Center.
sentences.zh: 现在回到萨顿西中心。

sentences.en: Thank you, Jeannie.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，珍妮。

sentences.en: You did a fine job.
sentences.zh: 你做得很好。

sentences.en: And here's Mike Sutton.
sentences.zh: 这是迈克·萨顿。

sentences.en: We're talking about...
sentences.zh: 我们正在谈论……

sentences.en: Sometimes the future falls open without a warning.
sentences.zh: 有时未来会毫无预兆地降临。

sentences.en: The earthquake, when it came, would knock people's lives off-kilter so brutally and abruptly that its power seemed to reverberate forever.
sentences.zh: 地震发生时，它如此残酷而突然地打乱了人们的生活，其力量似乎永远在回荡。

sentences.en: Some people, like Jeannie, would find their lives oriented differently in its aftermath.
sentences.zh: 有些人，像珍妮一样，会在灾后发现自己的人生方向发生了改变。

sentences.en: Others would find their entire worldview had changed.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则会发现他们的整个世界观都变了。

sentences.en: More than half a century later, an attorney in Anchorage would explain,
sentences.zh: 半个多世纪后，安克雷奇的一位律师解释说，

sentences.en: Even now I can look at this solid ground out my window and know it's not permanent.
sentences.zh: 即使现在，我看着窗外这片坚实的土地，也知道它并非永恒。

sentences.en: It can change any time.
sentences.zh: 它随时可能改变。

sentences.en: It just moves.
sentences.zh: 它只是在移动。

sentences.en: Everything moves.
sentences.zh: 万物皆在移动。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: This is who Jeannie was and where everything stood before what it stood on moved.
sentences.zh: 这就是珍妮是谁，以及在一切立足之地移动之前，一切所处的状态。

sentences.en: Friday, March 27th, 1964.
sentences.zh: 1964年3月27日，星期五。

sentences.en: The night of the earthquake.
sentences.zh: 地震发生的那个夜晚。

sentences.en: On the night of Good Friday, 1964,
sentences.zh: 1964年耶稣受难日的晚上，

sentences.en: I was writing a letter to a friend in Juneau.
sentences.zh: 我正在给朱诺的一位朋友写信。

sentences.en: Around 5.30,
sentences.zh: 大约5点30分，

sentences.en: Jeannie Chance sat at the typewriter in her bedroom, stealing some time alone before fixing dinner for her husband Winston and their three children.
sentences.zh: 珍妮·钱斯坐在卧室的打字机前，在为丈夫温斯顿和三个孩子准备晚餐前，偷得一点独处的时间。

sentences.en: Eight-year-old Jan,
sentences.zh: 八岁的简，

sentences.en: 11-year-old Albert, and 13-year-old Winston Jr., or Wins, who just then appeared at her bedroom door.
sentences.zh: 11岁的阿尔伯特，还有13岁的温斯顿二世（大家都叫他温斯），他就在这时出现在了卧室门口。

sentences.en: My son Wentz came to me and said that he just had to get down to the bookstore.
sentences.zh: 我儿子温斯走到我跟前说，他必须得去趟书店。

sentences.en: He'd forgotten to buy a copy of the Red Cross life-saving manual that he was supposed to bring to his swimming class the next morning.
sentences.zh: 他忘了买明天游泳课要用的红十字会救生手册。

sentences.en: And I said, please, for heaven's sakes, when you have to have something, don't wait until the last minute.
sentences.zh: 我说，求你了，看在老天的份上，当你需要什么东西时，别等到最后一刻才去买。

sentences.en: So Jeannie pulled on a pair of boots and a parka and headed out with Wins.
sentences.zh: 于是珍妮穿上靴子和派克大衣，带着温斯出发了。

sentences.en: So Wins and I got in the car and I was still in somewhat of an unhappy mood about having to make a last-minute errand downtown.
sentences.zh: 我和温斯上了车，因为不得不临时跑一趟市中心，我心里还是有点不痛快。

sentences.en: At 5.36, snow was falling as Jeannie and Wins headed downtown.
sentences.zh: 下午5点36分，珍妮和温斯前往市中心时，雪正在飘落。

sentences.en: The city was quiet.
sentences.zh: 城市很安静。

sentences.en: As they approached the intersection of C Street and 9th, the traffic light turned red.
sentences.zh: 当他们接近C街和第九大道的交叉路口时，交通灯变成了红色。

sentences.en: As I touched my brake, the car began to bounce.
sentences.zh: 当我踩下刹车时，车子开始颠簸起来。

sentences.en: The car started bucking.
sentences.zh: 车子开始剧烈摇晃。

sentences.en: So I said, oh no, and Wins says, what's the matter?
sentences.zh: 我说，噢不，温斯问，怎么了？

sentences.en: And I said,
sentences.zh: 我说，

sentences.en: I'll blow out.
sentences.zh: 爆胎了。

sentences.en: And Jeannie assumed she'd blown a tire.
sentences.zh: 珍妮以为是爆胎了。

sentences.en: And then it got worse.
sentences.zh: 接着情况变得更糟了。

sentences.en: She gripped the wheel.
sentences.zh: 她紧紧抓住方向盘。

sentences.en: Wins held on to his seat beside her.
sentences.zh: 温斯紧紧抓着身旁的座位。

sentences.en: For a moment, they bounced violently without speaking a word.
sentences.zh: 有一会儿，他们剧烈地颠簸着，一句话也没说。

sentences.en: Nothing was said between us for a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们沉默了几分钟。

sentences.en: And I said, you know, it's not a blowout.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道，这不是爆胎。

sentences.en: It must be a hard wind.
sentences.zh: 一定是强风。

sentences.en: And he says, boy, it's a wind, all right.
sentences.zh: 他说，天哪，这风可真够大的。

sentences.en: But the car bounced worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 但车子颠簸得越来越厉害。

sentences.en: And I lowered my window and I heard a banging,
sentences.zh: 我摇下车窗，听到一阵撞击声，

sentences.en: this clang banging, and looked across.
sentences.zh: 那种金属碰撞的叮当声，我向外看去。

sentences.en: And on one corner of the intersection...
sentences.zh: 在十字路口的一角……

sentences.en: Cars parked in a line were slamming into one another and separating again, like a grotesque accordion opening and closing.
sentences.zh: 停成一排的汽车像一把怪异的手风琴一样，不断地撞在一起又分开，一张一合。

sentences.en: I saw down the street to my left, two people holding on to each other trying to stand up.
sentences.zh: 我看到左边的街道上，有两个人互相搀扶着试图站起来。

sentences.en: Three people came...
sentences.zh: 三个人走过来……

sentences.en: The world and everything in it appeared to be convulsing.
sentences.zh: 世界以及其中的一切似乎都在抽搐。

sentences.en: Jeannie's eyes were seeing it, but her mind couldn't organize all this information into a coherent story.
sentences.zh: 珍妮的眼睛看到了这一切，但她的大脑无法将这些信息组织成一个连贯的叙述。

sentences.en: The car continued to bounce and bounce.
sentences.zh: 车子继续不停地颠簸。

sentences.en: Suddenly, she watched the road roll away from the car.
sentences.zh: 突然，她看着路面从车下翻滚开去。

sentences.en: Everybody crack, like it rolled.
sentences.zh: 所有东西都碎了，就像路面在翻滚一样。

sentences.en: As though some humpbacked shadow creature were surging under its surface, heading for town.
sentences.zh: 仿佛有一个驼背的阴影生物在路面下涌动，正向城里冲去。

sentences.en: Finally,
sentences.zh: 终于，

sentences.en: Jeannie found a word that could fasten together this chaos in her mind.
sentences.zh: 珍妮找到了一个词，能把她脑海中混乱的景象串联起来。

sentences.en: I said, whence this is an earthquake?
sentences.zh: 我说，温斯，这是地震吗？

sentences.en: Whence could only say, yeah.
sentences.zh: 温斯只能说，是的。

sentences.en: The Great Alaska Earthquake lasted four and a half minutes.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加大地震持续了四分半钟。

sentences.en: It overwhelmed people the way the strongest emotions do.
sentences.zh: 它像最强烈的情绪一样淹没了人们。

sentences.en: It was pure sensation, coming on faster than the intellect's ability to register it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种纯粹的感官体验，来得比大脑处理它的速度还要快。

sentences.en: It was amazing what details people noticed, the focal points their minds locked onto when the world went blurry.
sentences.zh: 当世界变得模糊时，人们注意到的细节和大脑锁定的焦点真是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: On 4th Avenue, a high school track star watched the window of a stationery store rattle and explode.
sentences.zh: 在第四大道，一名高中田径明星看着文具店的窗户嘎嘎作响并炸裂开来。

sentences.en: And he stood there, admiring the perfect, hurtling form of the man who came leaping out of it.
sentences.zh: 他站在那里，欣赏着那个从窗户跳出来的人那完美的腾空姿态。

sentences.en: At Presbyterian Hospital, one man watched blood seeping into the hall from under a doorway, like a scene in a horror movie.
sentences.zh: 在长老会医院，一名男子看着鲜血从门口渗入走廊，就像恐怖电影里的场景。

sentences.en: It took a second for him to realize that the hospital's blood bank had broken open and spilled.
sentences.zh: 他过了一秒才意识到是医院的血库破裂并洒了出来。

sentences.en: At the JCPenney department store, a 15-year-old in the elevator with some friends watched a book that one of them had dropped suddenly levitate off the floor and hang weightless
sentences.zh: 在杰西潘尼百货公司，一个15岁的孩子和朋友们在电梯里，看着其中一人掉落的一本书突然从地板上悬浮起来，失重地

sentences.en: in midair right in front of him.
sentences.zh: 悬在他面前的半空中。

sentences.en: For a split second, it was like they were in orbit.
sentences.zh: 那一瞬间，就像他们进入了轨道一样。

sentences.en: The elevator was falling.
sentences.zh: 电梯正在坠落。

sentences.en: But Jeannie's mind had already turned to reporting the news.
sentences.zh: 但珍妮的思绪已经转向了新闻报道。

sentences.en: As soon as it stopped, I looked up and I could see that our television tower was still standing.
sentences.zh: 地震一停，我抬头看去，发现我们的电视塔还立着。

sentences.en: She assumed her station would have power back on soon and that the 6 o'clock news broadcast would go on as usual.
sentences.zh: 她以为电视台很快就会恢复供电，6点的新闻广播会照常进行。

sentences.en: That meant she had less than 20 minutes to put together a story.
sentences.zh: 这意味着她只有不到20分钟的时间来整理新闻稿。

sentences.en: I knew we had no power by the fact that the traffic lights went out but I knew that our very ingenious engineers would have us on the air very shortly.
sentences.zh: 我知道停电了，因为交通灯灭了，但我知道我们那些非常有才华的工程师很快就会让我们恢复播出。

sentences.en: So Jeannie sped to the public safety building where the police and fire departments were headquartered to round up some details for a quick report.
sentences.zh: 于是珍妮驱车赶往公共安全大楼，那里是警察局和消防局的总部，她要去收集一些细节，准备一份简短的报道。

sentences.en: As I dashed in, I saw that all of their huge, heavy filing cabinets and desks were thrown face down on the floor.
sentences.zh: 当我冲进去时，看到他们所有巨大沉重的文件柜和办公桌都被掀翻在地。

sentences.en: and my son
sentences.zh: 还有我儿子

sentences.en: Wentz came running in the door and he yelled come quick
sentences.zh: 温斯跑进门大喊，快来，

sentences.en: Pennies is falling.
sentences.zh: 潘尼百货塌了。

sentences.en: Standing in the doorway of the public safety building they could see the brand new
sentences.zh: 站在公共安全大楼的门口，他们可以看到那座崭新的

sentences.en: J.C.
sentences.zh: 杰西

sentences.en: Penney department store.
sentences.zh: 潘尼百货公司。

sentences.en: The building was a point of pride in Anchorage.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑是安克雷奇的骄傲。

sentences.en: Pennies was one of the first major chain retailers to believe in Alaska enough to build in the state.
sentences.zh: 潘尼百货是第一批相信阿拉斯加并在此投资建店的大型连锁零售商之一。

sentences.en: But as I stood there and watched...
sentences.zh: 但当我站在那里看着……

sentences.en: But now, as Jeannie and Wentz watched through the flurrying snow...
sentences.zh: 但现在，当珍妮和温斯透过纷飞的雪花看着时……

sentences.en: The big slabs of concrete walls silently break loose and start toward the ground.
sentences.zh: 巨大的混凝土墙板无声地脱落，开始向地面坠去。

sentences.en: A tremendous concrete panel from the exterior started to swing away from the building as though on a hinge.
sentences.zh: 一块巨大的外墙混凝土板开始像装了铰链一样从建筑上摆脱出来。

sentences.en: And it fell to the street with a roar, that deafening roar.
sentences.zh: 它伴随着轰鸣声坠向街道，那震耳欲聋的轰鸣声。

sentences.en: With the facade peeled off, parts of the store were now open to the cold air, exposed like the rooms of a dollhouse.
sentences.zh: 随着外墙剥落，商店的部分区域现在暴露在寒冷的空气中，就像玩偶屋的房间一样。

sentences.en: And Wentz looked at me and I saw horror in his eyes.
sentences.zh: 温斯看着我，我在他眼中看到了恐惧。

sentences.en: All at once she registered the extent of the wreckage surrounding her.
sentences.zh: 她一下子意识到了周围破坏的程度。

sentences.en: A voice said something about people buried in the rubble.
sentences.zh: 有个声音说有人被埋在废墟里了。

sentences.en: A group of men came running down the street yelling,
sentences.zh: 一群人跑过街道大喊着，

sentences.en: Fourth Avenue is gone.
sentences.zh: 第四大道没了。

sentences.en: And behind them,
sentences.zh: 在他们身后，

sentences.en: Jeannie could see the roof of a familiar building resting on the street jabbed into the pavement at an incomprehensible angle.
sentences.zh: 珍妮可以看到一座熟悉建筑的屋顶停在街上，以一种不可思议的角度扎进路面。

sentences.en: Then was the first time that I thought the first thing I must do before I can go any further is get my family together and make sure everything is all right.
sentences.zh: 那是第一次，我想我能做的第一件事，在做任何进一步行动之前，就是把家人聚在一起，确保一切安好。

sentences.en: I wheeled out of there and headed home.
sentences.zh: 我调转车头，往家赶去。

sentences.en: Oh, before we got home I could see the house was still standing and I remember breathing out loud, thank God.
sentences.zh: 噢，在到家之前，我看到房子还立着，我记得我大声呼出一口气，谢天谢地。

sentences.en: As she pulled up,
sentences.zh: 当她停车时，

sentences.en: Jan and Albert shot out of the neighbor's house across the street.
sentences.zh: 简和阿尔伯特从街对面的邻居家冲了出来。

sentences.en: Wins leapt out of the car and ran to his sister and brother.
sentences.zh: 温斯跳下车，跑向他的姐姐和弟弟。

sentences.en: I said,
sentences.zh: 我说，

sentences.en: Pennies has fallen down and there's more damage downtown.
sentences.zh: 潘尼百货塌了，市中心还有更多破坏。

sentences.en: And Al then pulled off from me and he looked at me very soberly and he said,
sentences.zh: 阿尔伯特从我身边走开，非常严肃地看着我说，

sentences.en: I'm all right.
sentences.zh: 我没事。

sentences.en: Don't worry about me.
sentences.zh: 别担心我。

sentences.en: Go on and do your job.
sentences.zh: 去忙你的工作吧。

sentences.en: All three chance children began to understand without being told that their mother would be leaving again.
sentences.zh: 钱斯家的三个孩子开始明白，不用别人说，妈妈又要离开了。

sentences.en: Jeannie was proud of how self-sufficient her kids had become, but whatever pride she felt was undercut by guilt.
sentences.zh: 珍妮为孩子们变得如此独立而自豪，但无论她感到多么自豪，都被内疚感所削弱。

sentences.en: She knew her family was growing independent of her out of necessity because she wasn't around as much as other mothers and wives were.
sentences.zh: 她知道她的家庭因为需要而变得不再依赖她，因为她不像其他母亲和妻子那样经常陪伴在身边。

sentences.en: Down in the lower 48, the women's movement was underway, but Anchorage was 1,500 miles away from the rest of America.
sentences.zh: 在下方的48个州，妇女运动正在进行，但安克雷奇距离美国其他地区有1500英里远。

sentences.en: Feminism wasn't a word
sentences.zh: 女权主义并不是一个

sentences.en: Jeannie used.
sentences.zh: 珍妮会用的词。

sentences.en: Her struggle to balance work and family felt like a problem unique to her and isolated moments could trigger self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 她平衡工作和家庭的挣扎感觉像是她独有的问题，而孤立的时刻可能会引发自我怀疑。

sentences.en: At breakfast one morning, a few weeks earlier, the family was watching through the kitchen window as their neighbor scraped the ice off her husband's
sentences.zh: 几周前的一个早晨，吃早餐时，全家人透过厨房窗户看着邻居在刮掉她丈夫

sentences.en: Cadillac before he left for work.
sentences.zh: 凯迪拉克车上的冰，然后他才去上班。

sentences.en: This was the custom among many Anchorage wives, but in the chance home the roles were reversed.
sentences.zh: 这是许多安克雷奇妻子的习惯，但在钱斯家，角色是互换的。

sentences.en: Winston warmed up the car for Jeannie.
sentences.zh: 温斯顿为珍妮热车。

sentences.en: Now Winston asked her,
sentences.zh: 现在温斯顿问她，

sentences.en: Honey, if I get you a Cadillac like that, would you scrape the ice off and warm it up yourself?
sentences.zh: 亲爱的，如果我给你买辆那样的凯迪拉克，你会自己刮冰并热车吗？

sentences.en: There must have been a tinge of disgruntlement in his voice because before
sentences.zh: 他的语气里一定带着一丝不满，因为在

sentences.en: Jeannie could answer, eight-year-old
sentences.zh: 珍妮回答之前，八岁的

sentences.en: Jan interrupted to remind her father that he was actually very lucky.
sentences.zh: 简打断了她，提醒父亲他其实非常幸运。

sentences.en: It's not everyone who gets to warm up the car for Jeannie chance.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个人都能为珍妮·钱斯热车。

sentences.en: It was funny but uncomfortable and in hindsight it might feel ominous too since after the earthquake the more successful Jeannie became, the more
sentences.zh: 这很有趣但也让人不舒服，事后看来，这可能也预示着不祥，因为地震后，珍妮越成功，

sentences.en: Winston seethed.
sentences.zh: 温斯顿就越愤怒。

sentences.en: It was nearly six o'clock, about 20 minutes since the quake, the last half hour of daylight.
sentences.zh: 快六点了，距离地震大约20分钟，这是白天的最后半小时。

sentences.en: So I headed immediately back down to the downtown area still thoroughly confident we would be on the air in a very short time and I would have to have something to say.
sentences.zh: 所以我立即掉头回到市中心，依然完全确信我们很快就能恢复播出，而我必须得说点什么。

sentences.en: As Jeannie headed back downtown she kept her transistor radio tuned to
sentences.zh: 当珍妮回到市中心时，她一直把晶体管收音机调到

sentences.en: KE&I, hoping the station would be back on air in time for the hourly newscaSt.
sentences.zh: KE&I电台，希望电台能及时恢复播出，赶上整点新闻。

sentences.en: But so far nothing, only static.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止什么都没有，只有静电声。

sentences.en: Within minutes she was back at JCPenney.
sentences.zh: 几分钟内她就回到了杰西潘尼百货。

sentences.en: She parked and approached the store but stopped short in front of a slab of something in the snow.
sentences.zh: 她停好车走近商店，但在雪地里的一块东西前停下了脚步。

sentences.en: She stared at it, mesmerized and repulsed but couldn't place what it was.
sentences.zh: 她盯着它看，既着迷又反感，但无法辨认那是什么。

sentences.en: She remembered as a girl in Texas watching her father kill off his few remaining hogs after a snowstorm and hanging their fleshless hindquarters from the rafters of the barn.
sentences.zh: 她记得小时候在德克萨斯州，看着父亲在暴风雪后杀掉仅剩的几头猪，把它们没有肉的后腿挂在谷仓的椽子上。

sentences.en: This thing in the snow reminded
sentences.zh: 雪地里的这个东西让

sentences.en: Jeannie of that somehow.
sentences.zh: 珍妮不知为何想起了那个场景。

sentences.en: Finally a man shouted an explanation to her.
sentences.zh: 终于，一个男人向她喊出了答案。

sentences.en: It was half a woman he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，那是一个女人的半截身体。

sentences.en: He'd seen her get struck by the falling debris.
sentences.zh: 他看到她被坠落的碎片击中了。

sentences.en: Jeannie moved on quickly.
sentences.zh: 珍妮迅速走开了。

sentences.en: I went on over to 4th Avenue to survey the damage there so that I could make a report
sentences.zh: 我去了第四大道查看那里的破坏情况，以便能做一份报道，

sentences.en: and I was horrified to discover that two whole blocks had simply fallen into a crack that had opened up and there was no street under them.
sentences.zh: 我惊恐地发现，整整两个街区直接掉进了一个裂开的缝隙里，下面已经没有街道了。

sentences.en: For two whole blocks everything was wedged in a ragged chasm that had ripped open under the street.
sentences.zh: 整整两个街区的一切都被挤进了一个在街道下撕裂开来的参差不齐的深渊中。

sentences.en: 4th Avenue has just collapsed.
sentences.zh: 第四大道刚刚坍塌了。

sentences.en: It's just collapsed.
sentences.zh: 它刚刚坍塌了。

sentences.en: Soon an aftershock struck.
sentences.zh: 不久，余震发生了。

sentences.en: The windows of a bank started popping spraying glass across the sidewalk ahead of Jeannie as she headed back to her car.
sentences.zh: 银行的窗户开始爆裂，在珍妮返回车里的路上，玻璃碎片喷溅到人行道上。

sentences.en: Her transistor radio still tuned to
sentences.zh: 她的晶体管收音机依然调在

sentences.zh: KE&I电台，继续播放着静电声。

sentences.zh: 雪下得很大。

sentences.en: The sun was setting.
sentences.zh: 太阳正在落山。

sentences.en: The city going dark.
sentences.zh: 城市陷入了黑暗。

sentences.zh: 因为在那之后还有更多的箱子，很多很多，而在那些箱子里，

sentences.en: Jeannie lost her seat in the legislature to a slimy Californian transplant who ran a bare-knuckled campaign.
sentences.zh: 珍妮在议会中输给了一个卑鄙的加州移民，他进行了一场残酷的竞选。

sentences.en: Wins, the son who'd been with her in the car the evening of the quake, was diagnosed with cancer and died in 1990, just shy of his 40th birthday.
sentences.zh: 温斯，那个在地震当晚和她一起在车里的儿子，被诊断出患有癌症，并于1990年去世，离他40岁生日仅差几天。

sentences.en: And her other son, Al, was in and out of rehab and would die a few years after that.
sentences.zh: 她的另一个儿子，阿尔，进出康复中心，几年后也去世了。

sentences.en: Then Jeannie's second husband died.
sentences.zh: 然后珍妮的第二任丈夫去世了。

sentences.en: And as soon as he was gone,
sentences.zh: 他刚一离开，

sentences.en: Jeannie was hit by dementia.
sentences.zh: 珍妮就患上了痴呆症。

sentences.en: Hard.
sentences.zh: 非常严重。

sentences.en: That's why the boxes were there, unopened.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么箱子放在那里，没有打开。

sentences.en: Jeannie had packed them up, planning to write her autobiography, but she never got the chance.
sentences.zh: 珍妮把它们打包好，计划写自传，但她再也没有机会了。

sentences.en: I'll be honest, it was pretty depressing.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这相当令人沮丧。

sentences.en: I'd never heard of Jeannie Chance.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未听说过珍妮·钱斯。

sentences.en: I'd never even heard of the Great Alaska Earthquake.
sentences.zh: 我甚至从未听说过阿拉斯加大地震。

sentences.en: And it was unsettling that something so consequential, the most powerful earthquake in North America, could recede so invisibly into history.
sentences.zh: 令人不安的是，如此重大的事件——北美最强烈的地震——竟然能如此无声无息地退入历史。

sentences.en: To take in a stranger's entire life at that speed, blurred and compressed so dramatically, started to make me feel like maybe time itself was a slow-moving natural disaster
sentences.zh: 以这种速度去领略一个陌生人的一生，如此剧烈地模糊和压缩，开始让我觉得也许时间本身就是一场缓慢移动的自然灾害，

sentences.en: that eventually shakes everything apart.
sentences.zh: 最终将一切震得粉碎。

sentences.en: And from such a telescopic distance, it was impossible not to recognize the form that all our lives assume.
sentences.zh: 从如此遥远的距离看，不可能不认出我们所有生命所呈现的形式。

sentences.en: A forgettable blip, a meaningless straight line from birth to death.
sentences.zh: 一个可被遗忘的闪现，一条从出生到死亡毫无意义的直线。

sentences.en: At some point, sitting in that basement, I started picturing my own boxes in one of my own daughter's basements one day.
sentences.zh: 有那么一刻，坐在那个地下室里，我开始想象有一天我自己的箱子出现在我女儿的地下室里。

sentences.en: And then I imagine how many other sets of boxes are already out there, and how many people hadn't left boxes at all.
sentences.zh: 然后我想到还有多少其他人的箱子已经存在于世，以及有多少人根本没有留下箱子。

sentences.en: And maybe this part's harder to explain.
sentences.zh: 也许这部分更难解释。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel depressing to me now.
sentences.zh: 我现在并不觉得沮丧。

sentences.en: Because I also know that sealed inside this vulnerable little snow globe we call the present, life feels anything but forgettable and meaningless.
sentences.zh: 因为我也知道，被封存在我们称之为“当下”的这个脆弱的小雪球里，生活的感觉绝非易被遗忘或毫无意义。

sentences.en: And that recognizing the starkness of it all, the course our straight line is taking, liberates us into the present.
sentences.zh: 而意识到这一切的严峻性，意识到我们那条直线所行进的方向，反而让我们得以解脱，进入当下。

sentences.en: It imbues life with immediacy, just like a disaster does.
sentences.zh: 它赋予了生活一种紧迫感，就像灾难所带来的那样。

sentences.en: And just like disaster, it gives us the chance to expand those boundaries the only way we can.
sentences.zh: 而且就像灾难一样，它给了我们机会，以我们唯一能做到的方式去拓展那些边界。

sentences.en: By reaching out, by connecting our lives to the lives of others, by thatching our lines together, like a net.
sentences.zh: 通过伸出援手，通过将我们的生命与他人的生命相连，通过像编织网一样将我们的生命线交织在一起。
